palo_alto_traffic to OCSF pipeline.

functions.description: Parse PAN-OS CSV traffic log with named columns

add.value: generated_time || start_time || receive_time || undefined

functions.description: Alias captured timestamp field(s) to log_time (generated_time, start_time, receive_time) so _time reflects the source event, not pipeline processing time

findings.issue: OCSF field "actor.user.name" is defined for this class but empty in the output
OCSF field "device.hostname" is defined for this class but empty in the output

NAT destination IP (post-NAT) is used instead of the original destination IP. Source field 8 (175.16.199.1) is the NAT dst; field 7 is the original src, field 8 is original dst — mapping appears correct here but NAT dst IP (field 10: 175.16.199.1) and NAT src IP (field 9: 192.168.1.63) are entirely dropped and not mapped to nat_dst_endpoint / nat_src_endpoint
findings.example: nat_src_endpoint {ip:192.168.1.63} and nat_dst_endpoint {ip:175.16.199.1, port:443} missing from all events

findings.issue: Security policy/rule name (field 11: new_outbound_from_trust) present in source but not mapped — OCSF Network Activity expects firewall_rule.name
findings.example: new_outbound_from_trust present in every raw event, absent from all output events

findings.issue: Application name (field 14: apple-maps, ping, web-browsing, ssl, quic) is present in source but entirely dropped — should map to connection_info.boundary or app field
findings.example: apple-maps, ping, web-browsing, ssl, quic all absent from output

findings.issue: Traffic direction (from-policy / trust→untrust zones) is present and derivable but not mapped to connection_info.direction_id
findings.example: Zone pair trust→untrust and action from-policy present in source, missing in output

findings.issue: Firewall action (field 30: allow) is present in source but not mapped to OCSF disposition_id — this is a core OCSF Network Activity field
findings.example: action=allow in every raw event; disposition_id absent from all output events

findings.issue: Packet counts (fields 45/46: e.g. 16 pkts_sent, 20 pkts_rcvd for event 1) present in source but not mapped to traffic.packets_in / traffic.packets_out
findings.example: pkts_sent=16, pkts_rcvd=20 in event 1; absent from output

findings.issue: Total bytes (field 29: 7734) present in source but not mapped — only directional bytes mapped
findings.example: bytes=7734 in event 1 absent from output traffic object

findings.issue: Session start time (field 34: 2018/11/30 15:59:04) and elapsed time (field 35: 586 seconds) present in source but not mapped to OCSF start_time / duration
findings.example: start_time=2018/11/30 15:59:04, elapsed=586 in event 1; both absent from output

findings.issue: TCP end reason (field 44: tcp-fin, aged-out) and flags (field 28: 0x400053) are present but not mapped
findings.example: tcp-fin and 0x400053 in event 1; absent from output

findings.issue: Source and destination zones (fields 15/16: trust, untrust) present in source but not mapped to OCSF endpoint zone fields
findings.example: src_zone=trust, dst_zone=untrust in every event; absent from output

findings.issue: Ingress/egress interface names (fields 17/18: ethernet1/2, ethernet1/1) present in source but not mapped
Log receive time (field 2: 2018/11/30 16:09:07) differs from generate time and should populate metadata.logged_time or log_time; only one timestamp is captured
findings.example: receive_time=2018/11/30 16:09:07 vs generate_time=2018/11/30 16:09:07 — distinct field dropped

findings.issue: Device serial (field 3: 012801096514) and hostname (PA-220) present in source but device object is empty {} — should populate device.name and device.uid
findings.example: device:{} in every event; serial=012801096514, hostname=PA-220 present in source

findings.issue: Destination country (field 42: United States) present in source but not mapped to dst_endpoint.location.country
findings.example: dst_location=United States in every event; absent from output

findings.issue: Session ID (field 33: e.g. 22751) present in source but not mapped
findings.example: session_id=22751 in event 1; absent from output

findings.issue: URL category (field 36: computer-and-internet-info, web-advertisements, any) present in source but not mapped to any OCSF field
findings.example: url_category=computer-and-internet-info in event 1; absent from output

findings.issue: actor.user is populated as empty {} in every event — should be omitted if no user data exists in source rather than emitting an empty object
severity_id is hardcoded to 1 (Informational) without mapping from source — acceptable default but not derived from any source field
activity_id hardcoded to 1 for all events including end/allow actions — should reflect the subtype (e.g., Traffic End = 6 in OCSF 4001)
findings.example: activity_id:1 on all events though PA log type is 'end'

report.summary: The pipeline correctly maps the core IP/port 5-tuple, protocol, directional byte counts, and timestamp to valid OCSF Network Activity (class 4001) structure. However, the majority of information-rich fields present in the Palo Alto traffic log — firewall action/disposition, application name, NAT endpoints, packet counts, session start/duration, zones, interfaces, end reason, URL category, TCP flags, destination country, device identity, and session ID — are entirely dropped, representing a significant loss of the source data. The output skeleton is structurally valid OCSF but captures less than half of the available telemetry from these logs.
